paper.title_en: Analytic and Combinatorial Methods in Integrable Systems and Random Matrix Theory
paper.abstract_en: This thesis deals with the study of classical integrable systems. A system is said to be integrable if it possesses an inﬁnite number of conserved quantities. In this work, we study various examples of integrable systems, in particular those arising from random matrix models. Our focus is on the tau function, which characterizes an integrable system. We begin by exploring two types of integrable systems : discrete and continuous. Various analytical and combinatorial methods are employed. A tau function satisﬁes the Hirota equation, which gives rise to different partial differential equa-tions, such as the KP or KdV equations. From these tau functions, we deﬁne the correlators associated with an integrable system. Topological recursion provides the asymptotic expan-sion of these correlators. Our work spans several thematic areas. The approach we adopt is based on the Lax formalism, which we apply to random matrix models to derive our results. The aim of this thesis is to study the WKB expansion of the correlators associated with an integrable system.
